Schemes of National Horticultural
Board
*281. SHRI  MATILAL  SARKAR:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) the percentage of horticultural land
in the country, State-wise;
(b) the number of schemes implemented
by the National Horticultural Board
in the country and in the North-Eastern
States;
(c) the percentage of the horticultural
produce processed during the years
2002-03, 2003-04 and 2004-05; and
(d) whether Government are planning
for processing horticultural produce in a
larger quantity to avoid wastage of the
produce?
Sickle Cell disease in Chhattisgarh
*282. SHRIMATI MOHSINA
KIDWAI : Will the Minister of HEALTH
AND FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government are aware that
almost ten thousand people die in
Chhattisgarh due to Sickle Cell disease;
(b) whether Government would
consider establishing a Sickle Cell Unit in
the State to provide test facilities at all
district centres in Chhattisgarh; and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor and what
steps Government are taking to provide
cheap and reliable blood test alongwith the
details of facilities offered till date?
Pampa Action Plan
*283. PROF. P. J. KURIAN: Will the
Minister of ENVIRONMENT AND
FORESTS be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have approved
the Pampa Action Plan to clean and protect
the Pampa river in the State of Kerala;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) the present status of the action plan;
and
(d) in how much time the plan is
expected to be implemented fully?

Major rivers choked with industrial
effluents
*284. SHRI JANARDHANA
POOJARY: Will the Minister of
ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether a number of major rivers
and their tributaries are choking with
industrial effluents and other pollutants;
(b) if so, what are the details in this
regard and the programmes initiated by
Government to clean the rivers indicating
the amount spent thereon during the last
three years;
(c) whether it is a fact that heavy
discharge of sewage water in the Yamuna
River is creating havoc with the aquatic life
in the river and defeating the River
Conservation Plan; and
(d) if so, the details thereof and the
corrective steps taken in this regard?
Target for agricultural growth
*285. SHRI SANJAY RAUT: Will the
Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Government have set a
target to increase the annual growth rate of
agricultural production by more than
6.5 per cent of coming years;
(b) if so, the details of measures taken
or proposed to be taken for increasing
growth of agricultural products in the
country; and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
Medical and Dental colleges
*286. SHRI LALITBHAI MEHTA:
Will the Minister of HEALTH
AND FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to
state:
(a) the number of self-financed and
Government medical colleges and dental
colleges in the country, State-wise, and their
intake at 1st year M.B.B.S. level and
1st year of B.D.S.;
(b) whether it is a fact that many more
self-financed medical colleges and dental
colleges are in the pipeline;
(c) if so, the number of proposals
pending with the competent authorities;
and
(d) what is the action plan of his
Ministry for more dental and medical
colleges and to increase their intake?
Agenda of meeting of the National
Commission on Population

the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether the first meeting of the
recently constituted National Commission
on Population was held recently;
(b) if so, the agenda of the meeting and
its outcome thereof;
(c) whether any specific decisions were
taken to control the explosion of population
in the country, if so, the details thereof and
if not, the reasons therefor;
(d) whether it is a fact that the Prime
Minister announced during the meeting that
the Population Policy of the country does
not encourage incentives and disincentives;
and
(e) if so, the manner in which
Government propose to control  population
without any incentives and disincentives?

Displaying extent of pesticides on
labels of food items

SHRIMATI PREMA
CARIAPPA:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to refer
to the answer to Unstarred Question 499
given in the Rajya Sabha on the 4th March,
2005 and state:
(a) the reasons for which Government
do not wish to display extent of pesticides
on labels of food items by amending the
Food Adulteration (Prevention) Rules, 1955
keeping in view the concern for health of

pesticides have been found exceeding the
prescribed limit in several food products
and cold drinks and they affect the public
health adversely; and
(c) if so, by when Government would
make arrangements for display of the extent
of pesticides on the labels of food items?
Review of anti-poaching measures
*289. SHRI K.B. KRISHNA
MURTHY:
SHRI HARISH RAWAT:
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT
AND FORESTS be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have
conducted any comprehensive review of
the performance, particularly the anti-
poaching measures, in all the Reserves in
the country;
(b) if not, the reason therefor and
whether Government would conduct such
a review;
(c) if so, the details of the status of anti-
poaching measures in these reserves;
(d) what additional measures are being
taken to strengthen anti-poaching measures;
(e) whether Government are considering
setting up an expert group to monitor the
reserves; and
(f) if so, the details of its mandate?
Checking MRP violations
†*290. SHRI DILIP SINGH JUDEV:
Will the Minister of CONSUMER
AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC
DISTRIBUTION be pleased to state:
(a) the existing provision regarding
percentage of difference to be maintained
between actual cost and printed price in
regard to packaged consumer goods
including food items;
(b) the arrangements made for checking
this in order to prevent its violation;
(c) whether any action has been taken
by the Central Government on the
complaints received during the last three
years; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Growth rate of agriculture vis-a-vis
foodgrain stock
†*291. SHRI MANGANI LAL
MANDAL: Will the Minister of
AGRICULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) the percentage of targeted growth
rate of agriculture achieved during all the
years of Tenth Five Year Plan, so far,
alongwith the target fixed for growth rate
of agriculture for the remaining years and
the efforts being made to achieve the same;
and
(b) the status of storage of foodgrains
due to non-achieving the required and
intended growth rate of agriculture?

Infant mortality rate
*292. DR. K. MALAISAMY: Will the
Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the infant
mortality rate in India is much higher than
that of the neighbouring countries like
Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, etc.;
(b) if so, the details thereof in terms of
percentage and how it compares with
countries like Bangladesh, Nepal and Sri
Lanka;
(c) whether it is also a fact that India
tops in the births of under-weight babies
and neonatal mortality;
(d) the reasons for this alarming
situation;
(e) what is the Tenth Plan goal in these
areas; and
(f) what are the special measures in the
offing and undertaken to bring down these
problems?
Grants for protection of Sanctuaries
and Parks of Kerala
*293. SHRI A. VIJAYARAGHAVAN:
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT
AND FORESTS be pleased to state:
(a) whether any scheme for grant,
submitted for protecting Sanctuaries and
National Parks of Kerala, is under the
consideration of the competent authority;
(b) if so, the details including the grant
sought and the action taken on the above
proposal;
(c) the details of assistance sanctioned
to Kerala under the Scheme 'Development
of National Parks and Sanctuaries' during
the last three years, year-wise;
(d) whether steps will be taken to
increase the allocation to Kerala under the
said scheme;
(e) if so, the details thereof; and
(f) if not, the reasons therefor?
New policy for welfare of farmers
*294. SHRI N.R. GOVINDARAJAR:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the living condition of
farmers in our country is totally
unsatisfactory inspite of India emerging as
an agricultural power;
(b) if so, whether Government have
formulated/will formulate any new policy
for the welfare of farmers who are backbone
of our economy;
(c) if so, the salient features of the
policy;
(d) whether some reforms in the farm
sector are proposed to be introduced to
improve farmers' social and financial
conditions; and
(e) if so, the details thereof?
Population stabilization by co-
ordination with States
*295. SHRIMATI JAMANA DEVI
BARUPAL:
DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether Prime Minister has pruned
the National Commission on Population
from 131 to 44 members to ensure its more
effective functioning in achieving
population stabilization;
(b) whether the Commission will direct
implementation of policy with a view of
achieving population stabilization by

92
promoting synergy among demographic,
educational and environmental agencies,
etc.;
(c) whether the Commission has sought
to promote coordination in planning and
implementation of population policies
across the Central and State Government
agencies; and
(d) if so, upto what extent the
Commission is likely to achieve these aims
and objectives?
Ban on Indian Ayurvedic drugs by
Canada
*296. SHRIMATI BIMBA RAIKAR :
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether Canada has recently
imposed a ban on import of Indian
Ayurvedic formulations on the basis of
report of its drug testing labs alleging that
these Ayurvedic products contained high
levels of metals like lead, mercury, arsenic,
etc.;
(b) if so, whether the products such as
Shilajit, Kerala Capsules and
Mahasudarshan Churna have been declared
by Canadian authorities as unfit for human
consumption; and
(c) whether Government propose to
take up the  matter with the Canadian
Government for a possible reversal of its
ban order?
Non-availability of medicines in
CGHS dispensary, Laxmi Bai Nagar
†*297. SHRI BHAGWATI SINGH:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that special
medicines are not being indented by CGHS
dispensary No. 15, Laxmi Bai Nagar;
(b) if so, whether the main reason is
that the term of contract of the previous
supplier of indented medicines is over, thus
forcing CGHS beneficiaries to procure
medicines from open market;
(c) if so, the action taken in this regard;
and
(d) the details of pending bills of
pensioners, month-wise and by when such
bills would be cleared for payment?
Promoting inter-cropping
*298. SHRIMATI VANGA GEETHA:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have issued
an advisory to States for promoting best
farm practices to maximize production in
the ensuing kharif (paddy) season;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether it is a fact that Government
have called for inter-cropping for higher
returns and risk coverage to the farmers;
(d) if so, whether Government would
bear the risk if the farmers do not get
sufficient profits in changing their crops;
and
(e) if so, the proposed package of
reimbursement to be given to the farmers
in case they lose their crops due to these
reasons?
Connection of Hajira Port to its
hinterland
*299. SHRI LEKHRAJ BACHANI:
PROF. ALKA BALRAM
KSHATRIYA:
Will the Minister of RAILWAYS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether there is any need for
connecting Hajira Port to its hinterland;

Need of doctors and medical colleges
*300. SHRI JESUDASU SEELAM:
DR. T. SUBBARAMI
REDDY:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether there is shortage of doctors
in the country;
(b) whether the country needs to have
atleast a million doctors;

to manage with six lakh doctors, a shortfall
of four lakh doctors;

made, the nation may need upto 400
medical colleges in ten years to bridge this
gap;
